claim_formal: ∀ m≥1 ∃ simply connected closed Kähler M_m (dim_R 22) ∃ Hamiltonian H_m with all fixed points nondegenerate: #Fix(φ_{H_m}) = #Fix_0 = 80+1952m < SM(M_m) = 80+1968m (deficit unbounded)

quote_A.text: For every integer m ≥ 1, we construct a simply connected closed Kähler manifold with stable Morse number $`80+1968m`$ and a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with exactly $`80+1952m`$ fixed points

quote_B.text: The stable Morse formulation is stated explicitly in \cite[Conjecture~1.2]{Golovko2020}

notes: Headline = stable-Morse counterexamples (Golovko Conj 1.2); prefix ∀∃ reflects 'deficit unbounded', a single counterexample alone would be ∃. Other manuscripts: dim-1412 example (deficit 16), sharpness of cyclic integral Floer bound (dim 3332), Morse-number counterexample in dim 12, and quadric threefold with 3 fixed points (critical-number/cup-length Arnold bounds). Lean formalizes only the quadric Q^3 result (∃ φ with 3 fixed points < 4 = Crit), a secondary result.

claim_formal: ∀ connected closed Riemannian 4-manifold (M,g) with Ric=3g and sec≥0: universal cover ≅ round S^4, or Fubini–Study CP^2, or S^2(1/√3)×S^2(1/√3)

quote_A.text: Its universal Riemannian cover is one of the round $S^4$ of curvature $1$, the complex projective plane with its Fubini--Study metric normalized by $\operatorname{Ric}=3g$, or $S^2(1/\sqrt3)\times S^2(1/\sqrt3)$

quote_B.text: We prove the classification conjecture for connected smooth closed Einstein four-manifolds with strictly positive sectional curvature

notes: Headline (summary) is the nonnegative-curvature classification (corollary of zero-plane rigidity), which contains Yang's Conjecture 1 (strictly positive case, third manuscript); labelled P1/O1 via that conjecture, but the nonnegative statement itself may count as O8 extension. Lean formalizes only the strictly positive classification (special case) -> weaker. Companion L2 gap theorem is stated conditional on the classification premise (supplied by companion).

claim_formal: ∀ m≥2 ∀ closed connected M^m ∀ smooth minimal immersion F: M→S^{m+1}: F(M) not totally geodesic → Vol(M,F*g) ≥ a_m = min_k Vol(C_{k,m-k}) (attained by a Clifford product)

quote_A.text: The threshold is attained by a Clifford product minimizing \(a_m\).

quote_B.text: We prove the Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces of unit round spheres

notes: Also listed as Problem 31 in Yau's 1994 problem collection (could be P3); chose P1 because the modern formulation (Ge–Li Conj 1.12(ii)) names it a conjecture.

claim_formal: ∀ closed connected smooth Riemannian surface (M,g) ∃ C=C(M,g) ∀ λ>0 ∀ eigenfunction u≠0 with -Δu=λu: H^1(Z_u) ≤ C√λ

quote_A.text: There is a finite constant $C=C(M,g)$ such that every nonzero real Laplace eigenfunction ... obeys \[ \mathcal H_g^1(Z_u)\le C\sqrt\lambda. \]

quote_B.text: Together with the known lower bound, this proves Yau's conjecture in this setting.

notes: Yau's nodal conjecture posed in all dimensions; surfaces settled positively (O5), while other manuscripts refute the upper bound in dims 3, 4 (unbounded ratio) and 5 (power-law excess) — family as a whole is close to O3. Order √λ is sharp given Brüning's lower bound, so M9 is a defensible alternative. Lean SharpNodal.Main matches the headline; other Lean comparators cover the counterexamples.

claim_formal: ∀ closed 4-manifold M ∀ smooth Ricci flow g(t), 0≤t<T<∞: sup_{M×[0,T)}|R| < ∞ → g extends smoothly to [0,T+ε) on M

quote_A.text: If \[ \sup_{M\times[0,T)}|R(g(t))|<\infty, \] then there are \(\varepsilon>0\) and a smooth Ricci flow \(\widetilde g(t)\) on \(M\), \(0\le t<T+\varepsilon\), such that \(\widetilde g(t)=g(t)\)

quote_B.text: This resolves the scalar-curvature extension problem in dimension four.

notes: Prefix could be read ∀∃ (∃ extension ε, g̃). Scalar-curvature extension conjecture posed in all dimensions: companion disproves it in high dimension (S^2×S^{q+1}, q≥10), so the family overall resembles O3 (refute + corrected statement); headline dim-4 result labelled O5. Third manuscript is a technical tree inequality.

claim_formal: ∃ smooth U(10)-invariant Kähler form ω_0 ∈ [ω_FS] on CP^10 whose maximal Calabi flow exists on [0,T_*) with 0<T_*<∞ and S(ω(t))(p) ~ a(T_*-t)^{-1/2}

quote_A.text: There is a smooth \(U(10)\)-invariant K\"ahler form \(\omega_0\) on \(\CP^{10}\), in the class \([\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}]\), whose maximal smooth Calabi flow has existence interval \([0,T_*)\) with \(0<T_*<\infty\)

quote_B.text: This disproves Chen's smooth long-time existence conjecture, even in a class containing a constant-scalar-curvature metric.

notes: Corollary: singularities in every complex dimension ≥10 via products.

claim_formal: ∀ n∈{3,…,9} ∀ convex Ω⊂R^n ∀ u∈C^∞(Ω) with D²u>0, affine maximal, graph complete for induced Euclidean metric: Ω=R^n ∧ u is a quadratic polynomial (elliptic paraboloid)

quote_A.text: then \(\Omega=\R^n\) and \[ u(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Ax+b\cdot x+c \] for a positive-definite symmetric matrix \(A\)

quote_B.text: We prove the Euclidean-complete affine Bernstein conjecture in dimensions three through nine

notes: Rigidity statement; M6 (one-class classification) is an alternative. Smooth nonquadratic entire example in dimension 10 (companion) shows the range is sharp, so the family as a whole settles the dimension question (could be read O3/O1). Affine-complete corollary via Trudinger–Wang.

claim_formal: ∀ V∈(0,1): min perimeter among finite-perimeter sets of volume V in R^3/Z^3 = min{(36π)^{1/3}v^{2/3}, 2√(πv), 2} (v=min(V,1-V)), and the minimizers are exactly balls / tubes about shortest geodesics / slabs (or complements), transitions at 4π/81 and 1/π

quote_A.text: the minimum perimeter is \begin{equation} I_{\rm unit}(V)= \min\left\{(36\pi)^{1/3}v^{2/3},\ 2\sqrt{\pi v},\ 2\right\}

quote_B.text: We prove the isoperimetric conjecture for the cubic flat three-torus and classify all minimizers

notes: Exact profile (M9) plus full classification of minimizers (M6); chose M9 as primary.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth compact connected embedded surface M_0⊂R^3 ∀ singular point (x_0,T) at the first singular time ∃ smooth embedded self-shrinker S: the full rescaled family λ(M_{T+λ^{-2}s}-x_0) → √(-s)·S locally smoothly, multiplicity one, as λ→∞

quote_A.text: At every singular point $(x_0,T)$ at its first singular time there is a smooth properly embedded self-shrinker $S$ such that, as $\lambda\to\infty$, the full family ... converges

quote_B.text: \Cref{thm:main} establishes the negative-time part of that fixed-center uniqueness assertion at the first singular time

notes: Uniqueness of tangent flows; existence of the limit S makes M2 an alternative. Problem from Haslhofer 2025 (Problem 5.1, Conjecture 5.2) per the manuscript's introduction (main .tex consulted); settled only at the first singular time and for negative times -> O5. quote_B is from the manuscript's introduction.tex (beyond the truncated input intro).

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2 ∀ κ∈R ∀ complete separable metric space (M,d): (M,d) is n-dim Alexandrov with curv ≥ κ ⇔ (M,d,H^n) is full-support RCD((n-1)κ,n) with distributional sectional curvature ≥ κ in Gigli's global test classes

quote_A.text: Let \(n\ge2\) be an integer, let \(\kappa\in\R\), and let \((M,d)\) be a complete separable metric space. The following conditions are equivalent.

quote_B.text: This resolves Gigli's characterization conjecture in dimensions at least two.

notes: Lean WeakHessian formalizes the auxiliary 'weak Hessian bounds along every geodesic' theorem (companion manuscript), not the characterization.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2 ∃ L_n ∀ K∈R ∀ noncollapsed RCD(K,n) space (X,d,H^n) ∀ p∈X with all tangents Euclidean ∃ open U∋p, open V⊂R^n, homeomorphism F:U→V that is L_n-bi-Lipschitz for d

quote_A.text: there exist an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(p\), an open set \(V\subset\R^n\), and a homeomorphism \(F:U\to V\) such that \[ L_n^{-1}d(x,z)\le |F(x)-F(z)|\le L_nd(x,z)

quote_B.text: We resolve the regular-point bi-Lipschitz conjecture in the noncollapsed setting.

notes: Full prefix is ∀∃∀∃ (∀n ∃L_n ∀X ∀p ∃U,F); summary says constant is point-dependent while the paper gives L_n depending only on n. 'In the noncollapsed setting' may make it O5 if the conjecture is posed for general RCD.

claim_formal: ∃ closed connected orientable smooth 3-manifold M: (∃ C^∞ metric on M without conjugate points) ∧ ¬(∃ C^∞ metric on M with sec ≤ 0)

quote_A.text: There exists a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold $M$ with a $C^\infty$ Riemannian metric without conjugate points, such that $M$ admits no $C^\infty$ Riemannian metric whose sectional curvature is everywhere at most zero.

quote_B.text: This question appears in Ivanov and Kapovitch \cite[Questions~1.1 and~8.1]{IvanovKapovitch2014} ... We give a negative answer in dimension three

notes: Uses Leeb's graph-manifold obstruction; main work is the no-conjugate-points metric.

claim_formal: ∃ contractible domain M⊂C^3 ∃ complete Kähler g on M ∃ 0<A≤B: -B ≤ K_g ≤ -A ∧ no bounded holomorphic F:M→C^3 has nowhere-vanishing Jacobian (so M is not biholomorphic to a bounded domain)

quote_A.text: There exist a contractible domain $M\subset\C^3$, a smooth complete K\"ahler metric $g$ on $M$, and finite constants $0<A\le B$ such that \[ -B\le K_g(\sigma)\le -A<0 \]

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to the negatively pinched Kähler uniformization question.

notes: Question = Wu–Yau Conjecture 4.3 (also Wu 1967 question), hence P1 (P2 also defensible). Second manuscript: one-sided curvature ≤ -1 example with only constant bounded holomorphic functions (Yau Problem 38 question), also negative.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth connected compact boundaryless (M,g), dim ≥2, satisfying weak MTW: ∀ x∈M, the tangent injectivity domain I(x) is convex

quote_A.text: If $(M,g)$ satisfies \eqref{eq:weak-mtw}, then $I(x)$ is convex for every $x\in M$.

quote_B.text: implies convexity of every tangent injectivity domain, resolving Villani's conjecture in this setting

notes: 'In this setting' (compact manifolds) could signal O5 if Villani posed it more generally. Companion: uniform bi-Hölder optimal transport maps over density-bounded classes (also Lean-formalized).

claim_formal: ∀^∞ k ∃ complete smooth metric g_k on R^3 with Ric ≥ 0: h_k(R^3,g_k) ≥ (k+2)^2 > (k+1)^2 = h_k(R^3,g_E)

quote_A.text: For every sufficiently large integer k, a complete smooth metric on ℝ3 has at least $`(k+2)^2`$ independent harmonic functions of growth at most k, exceeding the Euclidean count $`(k+1)^2`$.

quote_B.text: This answers Yau's integer-degree dimension comparison question negatively in dimension three

notes: Paper states h_k ≥ c(k+1)^2 for c<9v/4, k ≥ k_0(v,c). Lean (HarmonicGrowth) formalizes the other manuscript's statement (∃ even n≥8, k≥2, g) and is proved by an axiom; it is a different counterexample, not a special case of the 3-dim headline.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth admissible datum (f_0,E_0,B_0) for 3D one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell ∃! global classical solution, C^∞ on [0,T] with compact phase-space support for every finite T

quote_A.text: Every smooth admissible datum \eqref{eq:data} generates a unique global classical solution of \eqref{eq:rvm}.

quote_B.text: This resolves the large-data global classical regularity problem for this model, without size or symmetry restrictions on the data.

notes: Well-known open problem (Glassey–Strauss program) rather than a named conjecture.

claim_formal: ∃ nonnegative F_0 on T^3×R^3 (bounded velocity support, finite mass, energy, |entropy|) ∃ two distinct global entropy solutions of hard-sphere Boltzmann with exact local conservation of mass, momentum and energy, both in C([0,∞);L^1)

quote_A.text: There exist \(R<\infty\) and a nonnegative datum \(F_0\) ... for which \eqref{eq:collision} has two global entropy solutions with local conservation

quote_B.text: Existence and weak stability do not supply uniqueness. The uniqueness problem for general renormalized solutions is discussed

notes: Nonuniqueness = negative answer to the uniqueness question (tie-break 5 -> M3; M2 also plausible). Lean formalizes the earlier manuscript's admissible class (local mass + total momentum, energy inequality), a weaker conservation class than the headline.

claim_formal: ∀ stable finite-range radial potential Φ ∀ C^1 density f_0 with Gaussian bounds ∀ T such that Boltzmann has a classical solution with uniform Gaussian bound on [0,T] ∀ s≥1: lim_{ε→0} sup_{t≤T} ||F_s^ε(t) - f(t)^{⊗s}||_{L^1} = 0

quote_A.text: every fixed integer $s\ge1$ satisfies \begin{equation}\label{intro:chaos} \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\; \sup_{0\le t\le T} \bigl\|F_s^\varepsilon(t)-f(t)^{\otimes s}\bigr\|_ {L^1((\R^3\times\R^3)^s)}=0.

quote_B.text: We prove this limit for stable finite-range radial potentials on every finite interval where the Boltzmann solution has the regularity and Gaussian bound specified below.

notes: Extends Lanford/Pulvirenti–Saffirio–Simonella (short time) and Deng–Hani–Ma (hard spheres, full regular lifespan) to stable radial potentials; no explicitly named conjecture, so P2/O8 is a judgement call (O1 if 'long-time derivation for potentials' is taken as the posed problem). Companion: finite-dimensional hard-sphere Gaussian fluctuations (CLT) on the regular lifespan.

claim_formal: ∀ compact connected M^n (n≥3) with boundary ∀ nonempty open Γ⊂∂M ∀ smooth (g_1,A_1),(g_2,A_2) (metric, u(2)-connection on M×C^2): Λ_{g_1,A_1,Γ}=Λ_{g_2,A_2,Γ} → ∃ diffeo Φ (Φ|_Γ=id) ∃ U:M→U(2) (U|_Γ=I): g_2=Φ*g_1 ∧ A_2=U^{-1}(Φ*A_1)U+U^{-1}dU

quote_A.text: then there are a smooth diffeomorphism $\Phi:M\longrightarrow M$ and a smooth map $U:M\longrightarrow U(2)$ such that ... $g_2=\Phi^*g_1$

quote_B.text: We resolve the smooth anisotropic Calderón uniqueness problem with arbitrary same-patch measurements.

notes: Uniqueness up to gauge (the ∃Φ,U are the gauge witnesses), so M1 with ∀∃; M7 also arguable. Headline is the joint metric+connection theorem, which contains the companion's resolution of the smooth anisotropic Calderón problem (Lee–Uhlmann; could be P1). Third manuscript: nonuniqueness for bounded measurable scalar conductivities in 3D; Lean (Conductivity) formalizes only that counterexample.

claim_formal: ∀ bounded Lipschitz Ω⊂R^2 ∀ g∈L^∞ ∀ reduced absolute Mumford–Shah minimizer (u,K) ∀ x∈K: near x, K is a C^{1,α} arc through x, or a C^{1,α} arc ending at x, or three C^{1,α} arcs meeting at x at 120°; and ∀ U⋐Ω only finitely many components of K meet U

quote_A.text: Every $x\in K$ has an interior neighborhood in which $K$ has one of the following forms, with $C^{1,\alpha}$ arcs for some $\alpha>0$

quote_B.text: We prove the interior regularity assertion of the planar Mumford–Shah conjecture for reduced absolute minimizers with bounded fidelity data.

notes: Local classification of the discontinuity set (M6; M1 'regularity' also plausible). 'Interior regularity assertion' only; boundary behaviour not claimed, possible O5 reading. Corollary: ∇u ∈ weak-L^4_loc.

claim_formal: d_* = 7, i.e. (∀ d≤6 ∀ nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer u of the one-phase Bernoulli energy on R^d: u is flat) ∧ (∃ nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer on R^7)

quote_A.text: Every nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer of \eqref{eq:energy} in \(\R^d\), \(1\leq d\leq6\), is flat. There is a nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer in \(\R^7\). Consequently, \[ d_*=7. \]

quote_B.text: Our main result answers positively the critical-dimension question whether $d_*=7$.

notes: d_* is a pre-named number (tie-break 1 -> none; ∀ for the d≤6 part). Known bounds 5 ≤ d_* ≤ 7 (Jerison–Savin, De Silva–Jerison), so P4 also plausible; exact determination -> O1/M9 per tie-break 7. Existence in R^7 is De Silva–Jerison's; Lean formalizes only that half (nonflat_in_seven) -> weaker. Corollary: singular set dim ≤ n-7, sharp.

claim_formal: ∀ p∈[1,∞) ∀ bounded domains Ω,Λ⊂R^3 ∀ homeomorphism f:Ω→Λ in W^{1,p} ∃ C^∞ diffeomorphisms f_j:Ω→Λ with f_j→f strongly in W^{1,p}

quote_A.text: There exist $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms $f_j:\Omega\to\Lambda$, each belonging to $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\R^3)$, such that \begin{equation}\label{main:convergence} \int_\Omega\bigl( |f_j-f|^p+|Df_j-Df|^p\bigr)\,dx\longrightarrow0.

quote_B.text: We resolve the three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem for $`1\le p\le2`$.

notes: Two manuscripts (1≤p≤2 and p>2) combine to the full range. Ball–Evans question comes from Ball's open-problems discussion (not a numbered list, so P2). Dimension 3 is the case singled out (planar case known, n≥4 has counterexamples for small p); if the problem is read as posed in all dimensions, tie-break 6 gives O5.

claim_formal: ∀ bounded simply connected Ω⊂R^2 with C^∞ boundary ∀ u≠0 in the first positive Neumann eigenspace ∀ x∈Ω: ∇u(x)≠0 (hence min_{∂Ω}u < u(x) < max_{∂Ω}u)

quote_A.text: For every $0\ne u\in\V$, \[ \grad u(x)\ne0\qquad(x\in\Omega). \]

quote_B.text: We prove the strict hot spots conjecture for smooth bounded simply connected planar domains.

notes: Burdzy 2005 Conjecture 1.2(ii). Smoothness of the boundary is an added hypothesis relative to general (e.g. Lipschitz) simply connected domains; possible O5 reading.

quote_A.text: There are no functions \[ u,v\in C^2(\R^n\setminus\{0\})\cap C(\R^n), \qquad u(x)>0,\quad v(x)>0\quad(x\in\R^n), \] satisfying Equation~\eqref{eq:system}

quote_B.text: We prove the subcritical Hénon–Lane–Emden conjecture

notes: Resolves Huang–Zou Conjecture B; corollary: unweighted Lane–Emden conjecture. Phan's Conjecture C in full only by combining with Bidaut-Véron–Giacomini's radial existence theorem.

claim_formal: ∃^∞ odd p ∃ k>8 ∃ nonempty open U⊂H^k(T^12): ∀ u_0∈U the defocusing NLS i u_t+Δu=|u|^{p-1}u blows up in finite time T (no H^k continuation; self-similar rate (T-t)^{-1/(p-1)})

quote_A.text: There exist an odd integer $p\geq3$, a finite integer $k>8$, and a nonempty open set $\mathcal U\subset H^k(\mathbb T^{12};\mathbb C)$ with the following property.

quote_B.text: Thus finite-time blowup is stable under Sobolev perturbations in this supercritical regime.

notes: Lean stable_blowup is ∀p₀ ∃p≥p₀ ..., i.e. infinitely many powers; paper states ∃p ('can be chosen sufficiently large'), so prefix ∃ also defensible. Matrix: M2 (existence of an open blowup set) vs M3 (negative answer to defocusing supercritical global regularity); Gaussian corollary explicitly refutes a universal almost-sure global existence assertion motivated by Deng–Nahmod–Yue Open problem 3. Posed problem is not explicitly named, so B is uncertain.

claim_formal: ∀ bounded connected Ω⊂R^3 with C^∞ boundary ∀ smooth (λ_j,μ_j), μ_j>0, 3λ_j+2μ_j>0 on Ω̄ (j=1,2): Λ_{λ_1,μ_1}=Λ_{λ_2,μ_2} → λ_1=λ_2 ∧ μ_1=μ_2

quote_A.text: If \[ \Lambda_{\lambda_1,\mu_1} =\Lambda_{\lambda_2,\mu_2} ... \] then $\lambda_1=\lambda_2$ and $\mu_1=\mu_2$ throughout $\Omega$.

quote_B.text: This resolves the smooth three-dimensional isotropic elastic Calderón uniqueness problem under these positivity assumptions.

notes: Injectivity of the displacement-to-traction map; earlier claimed by Nakamura–Uhlmann 1994 but corrected in 2003 to a small-gradient case, so not O9.

claim_formal: ∃ ρ∈C_c^∞(R^3) probability density with √ρ∈C_c^∞: E(μ)<∞ is attained by a coupling, ∀ measure-preserving Borel T_2,T_3: ∫c(x,T_2x,T_3x)dμ > E(μ), and Monge inf = Kantorovich min

quote_A.text: every pair of Borel maps \(T_2,T_3:\R^3\to\R^3\) satisfying \((T_2)_\#\mu=(T_3)_\#\mu=\mu\) obeys \[ \int_{\R^3}c\bigl(x,T_2(x),T_3(x)\bigr)\dd\mu(x)>\E(\mu). \]

quote_B.text: The three-particle Coulomb question in \(\R^3\) was still stated as open in January 2026 by Friesecke

notes: Counterexample to the Monge/co-motion ansatz. Also: same nonattainment for every Riesz exponent s>0 in each d≥2.

claim_formal: ∀ d≥2 ∀ compact convex K⊂R^d with interior ∀ nonempty compact Y ∃ C(K,Y) ∀ μ,ν∈P(Y): ||T_μ-T_ν||_{L^2(ρ_K)} ≤ C·W_2(μ,ν)^{1/3}, and 1/3 cannot be improved (three-atom targets on a cube)

quote_A.text: \|T_\mu-T_\nu\|_{L^2(\rho)} \le C(K,Y)\,W_2(\mu,\nu)^{1/3} ... The exponent \(1/3\) cannot be replaced by any larger exponent in general

quote_B.text: A three-atom family on a fixed cube disproves Letrouit's conjectured uniform square-root estimate.

notes: Refutes Letrouit's conjectured exponent 1/2 and determines the sharp exponent 1/3 -> O3 (tie-break 7). Explicit admissible constant obtained in the paper (effective). Lean has both the stability bound and the sharpness theorem.

quote_A.text: Then there are $e\in\mathbb S^7$ with $e_8>0$ and $c\in\R$ such that \[ u(x)=\tanh\!\left(\frac{e\cdot x-c}{\sqrt2}\right)

quote_B.text: We resolve De Giorgi's conjecture positively in dimension eight

notes: Rigidity/one-dimensional symmetry (M1; M6 alternative). Dimension 8 is the endpoint of the conjecture (posed for n ≤ 8) and lower dimensions follow by adding dummy variables, hence O1 rather than O5. Stronger result: stable solutions in R^7 are 1D or constant, without energy-growth assumption.

claim_formal: ∃ algorithm A ∀ deterministic Turing machine M ∀ input w: f=A(M,w) is a smooth (mean-zero, optionally solenoidal) force on flat T^3 such that NS from rest at fixed computable ν>0 has a unique global smooth solution and the particle from a_* enters O at some finite time ⇔ M halts on w (so the particle event is undecidable)

quote_A.text: There is an algorithm taking a deterministic single-tape machine $M$ and a finite word $w$ to an effective smooth mean-zero force $f_{M,w}$ ... The particle initially at $a_*=(1/8,3/8,0)$ enters ... if and only if $M$ halts on $w$.

quote_B.text: Can a finite program for an external force make that particle enter the region exactly when a given Turing machine halts? ... We prove this for an explicit family of smooth forces.

notes: Turing universality of forced NS particle reachability; undecidability is a corollary. Nothing explicitly posed (self-posed question), so P5; outcome codes fit poorly — O8 chosen because it extends Euler/Hodge-viscous fluid-computation results to forced NS on a flat domain from rest ('other' also defensible). Many variant manuscripts (eventually stationary, rapidly vanishing, periodic forcing, velocity-field detection). Lean comparators formalize several variants (e.g. balanced three-stack on R^3).

quote_A.text: For every integer $d\ge3$ there are constants $\alpha_d\in(0,1/3]$ and $C_d<\infty$ such that every bounded infinity-harmonic function $u\in C(B_1)$ ... belongs to $C^{1,\alpha_d}(B_{1/2})$

quote_B.text: In particular, infinity-harmonic functions are locally C1 on every open subset of ℝd, for d ≥ 3.

notes: Regularity statement with a quantitative estimate (M8 alternative). Exponent from compactness, not explicit (ineffective). Settles the C^1 / C^{1,α} regularity question in d≥3 (planar case known from Savin, Evans–Savin); does not reach the conjectured sharp 1/3 exponent.
